papers.title: A Preconditioned Quantum Linear Solver for Periodic Two-Phase Heat Conduction with Mesh-Independent Condition Number
papers.abstract: We consider here computational homogenization of a periodic two-phase conduction problem. Quantum linear-system algorithms for its finite element discretization are limited by the condition number of the stiffness matrix. This condition number grows quadratically with the number of elements per side. Classically, preconditioning by the homogeneous (single-phase) operator bounds the condition number by the conductivity contrast, for every mesh size. On a quantum computer, however, a preconditioner encoded as a separate factor multiplies the subnormalizations, and the quadratic dependency returns. In this paper, we absorb the closed-form inverse square root of the homogeneous operator into the finite element factors. The preconditioned operator then becomes the product of a norm-preserving gradient operator $\mat{V}$, a diagonal matrix of scaled conductivities, and $\mat{V}^T$. Each factor has norm at most one. The block encoding therefore has subnormalization one, and its condition number is bounded by just the conductivity contrast, for every mesh size and in every dimension. The operator $\mat{V}$ is applied as a quantum Fourier transform, a small rotation at each wavenumber, and an inverse transform. Quantum singular value transformation then block-encodes the inverse of the preconditioned operator. We test the method numerically on three periodic cells with up to $10^6$ unknowns. The results confirm that the condition number does not depend on the mesh, and the energy-norm error of the inverse is below the polynomial tolerance at every mesh. On meshes of $4 \times 4$ and $8 \times 8$ elements, we also build the entire inverse as one Qiskit circuit and simulate it by state vector, with the rotation at each wavenumber built from uniformly controlled rotations. The output state agrees with the finite element solution to within the polynomial tolerance.

papers.title: A Good-Vorticity Low-Regularity Integrator for the Inviscid Oldroyd--B System with Stress Diffusion
papers.abstract: We establish sharp convergence results for a sequential semi-implicit good-vorticity integrator for the two-dimensional inviscid Oldroyd--B system with stress diffusion on the torus. For exact solutions satisfying $u\in C_tB^{1+\alpha}_{\infty,1}$ and $\tau\in C_tB^\alpha_{\infty,1}\cap L^1_tB^{2+\alpha}_{\infty,1}$, $0\le\alpha\le2$, we prove convergence in the critical norms $B^1_{\infty,1}\times B^0_{\infty,1}$, uniformly over the time nodes on every finite interval where these regularity assumptions hold, including the critical endpoint $\alpha=0$. For $0<\alpha\le2$, we obtain the rate $O(h^{\alpha/2})$ without any additional time H\"older assumption, reaching first order at $\alpha=2$. These algebraic exponents are optimal for this Eulerian scheme over the stated solution classes, as shown by fixed-data lower bounds in the case $a=b=0$ with nonzero velocity mean. For a fixed shear solution at critical regularity, we establish matching logarithmic upper and lower bounds on the numerical error, ruling out every positive algebraic convergence rate. We also prove that the gain of one stress derivative at the time nodes is optimal when the velocity is controlled in $B^1_{\infty,1}$, even for smooth initial stress.

papers.title: Immersed Boundary Electrodiffusion in the Wasserstein Gradient Flow Formalism: Global Well-Posedness, Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamics, and Singular Asymptotics
papers.abstract: We introduce a unified optimal transport framework for the Immersed Boundary (IB) electrodiffusion active pump model. By representing membrane chemical potential barriers and active pump potentials via smoothed Eulerian kernels ($\Psi_w, \mathcal{H}_w$), we formulate the passive dynamics as an $L^2$-Wasserstein ($W_2$) gradient flow coupled to non-conservative active pushing fields representing ATP-driven $3:2$ $\text{Na}^+/\text{K}^+$ exchangers. We establish global weak existence of solutions to the continuous Poisson--Nernst--Planck--IB system via a split-step Jordan--Kinderlehrer--Otto (JKO) variational scheme, backed by Calder\'on--Zygmund bounds for non-local Poisson drift and $H^3(\mathbb{S}^1)$ interface regularity under Stokes flow. We prove the continuous Rayleighian energy balance and establish exponential $W_2$-stability of Non-Equilibrium Steady States (NESS) under a quantitative Bakry--\'Emery curvature threshold. Furthermore, we analyze the dual singular limits of kernel smoothing width $w \to 0$ and dimensionless Debye length $g = \lambda_D / L \to 0$. We establish the precise asymptotic regime connecting regularized and sharp models, prove the $\Gamma$-convergence of regularized energy functionals, derive distributional interface flux jump conditions, and resolve $O(\lambda_D)$ Debye space-charge boundary layers to confirm bulk electroneutrality.

papers.title: On reduced SPDE models for stochastic Cucker-Smale flocking dynamics
papers.abstract: Flocking refers to a phenomenon in collective motion where particles align their velocities with each other, commonly modelled using Cucker-Smale dynamics. In this work, we introduce and analyse two general reduced SPDE models for stochastic Cucker-Smale particle dynamics that encompass environmental and i.i.d.-type noises. Our models are computationally cheaper alternatives to the underlying particle system and preserve the flocking behaviour. To derive our reduced models, we consider suitable empirical particle densities which depend on position and time, but feature velocity dependency in a multiplicative fashion: this setup crucially allows for a very intuitive and convenient notion of flocking at the SPDE level. In $d=1$ we prove flocking of the reduced SPDE models, and, for the environmental noise, we also quantify the discrepancy between the reduced SPDE and mollified particle system. We also discuss the technical modifications required to extend the results to higher dimensions. We then provide extensive numerical experiments to verify our theoretical results in $d=1$ and to explore the behaviour of our models in $d=2$.

papers.title: Dirichlet form approach to stochastic thin-film equations
papers.abstract: The thin-film equation describes the evolution of a thin liquid film driven by capillarity and limited by viscosity. For sufficiently small film heights, thermal fluctuations may not be neglected. Since the thin-film equation as an overdamped evolution equation has a gradient flow structure, the informal implementation of the fluctuation-dissipation principle is straightforward. In this paper, we work out that the concept of Dirichlet forms and the related construction of Markov processes are tailor-made for this type of overdamped continuum evolution with thermal noise. However, the concept of Dirichlet forms relies on the availability of a Gibbsian equilibrium measure, which, in case of the thin-film equation, limits the treatment to the $(1+1)$-dimensional case. By means of Dirichlet form theory, we obtain the existence and uniqueness of the evolution of laws on configuration space. We show that the regularity of the realizations of this Markov process matches the heuristics. In a simplified situation with a Gaussian reference measure and a non-degenerate mobility function, we characterize it as what is called an energy solution. The latter provides a pathwise decomposition of the driving forces into a deterministic and a thermal one, which was the starting point. Applying the same techniques in the spatially discretized setting proposed in [Math. Comp. 92 (2023), 1931--1976], we obtain the same results uniformly in the discretization parameter. In particular, Galerkin as well as spectral approximations of the stochastic thin-film equation are shown to be uniformly tight in optimal topologies. In the simplified setting, we also prove Mosco convergence of the associated Dirichlet forms and thereby obtain convergence of these approximations.

papers.title: Quantifying Concentration Phenomena of Mean-Field Transformers in the Low-Temperature Regime
papers.abstract: Transformers with self-attention modules as their core components have become an integral architecture in modern large language and foundation models. In this paper, we study the evolution of tokens in deep encoder-only transformers at inference time which is described in the large-token limit by a mean-field continuity equation. Leveraging ideas from the convergence analysis of interacting multi-particle systems, with particles corresponding to tokens, we prove that the token distribution rapidly concentrates onto the push-forward of the initial distribution under a projection map induced by the key, query, and value matrices, and remains metastable for moderate times. Specifically, we show that the Wasserstein distance of the two distributions scales like $\sqrt{{\log(\beta+1)}/{\beta}}\exp(Ct)+\exp(-ct)$ in terms of the temperature parameter $\beta^{-1}\to 0$ and inference time $t\geq 0$. For the proof, we establish Lyapunov-type estimates for the zero-temperature equation, identify its limit as $t\to\infty$, and employ a stability estimate in Wasserstein space together with a quantitative Laplace principle to couple the two equations. Our result implies that for time scales of order $\log\beta$, which correspond to the early-phase behavior most relevant for practical finite-depth models, the token distribution concentrates at the identified limiting distribution. Numerical experiments confirm this and, beyond that, complement our theory by showing that for finite $\beta$ and large $t$ the dynamics enter a different terminal phase, dominated by the spectrum of the value matrix.

papers.title: Sharp Nonlocal Poincar\'e Inequalities and Liminf Lower Bounds for Sobolev and BV Energies on Metric Measure Spaces
papers.abstract: Let $p\in[1,\infty)$, and let $(X,\rho,\mu)$ be a complete doubling $q$-Poincar\'e space for some $q\in[1,p]$ with a lower dimension $d$ and an upper dimension $D$. In this article, we establish Poincar\'e inequalities for two families of nonlocal nonconvex functionals defined using distances or volumes. More precisely, for any ball $B$ with its radius $r_B\in(0,\operatorname{diam} X)$, any $\lambda\in(0,\infty)$, and any measurable function $f:X\to\mathbb R$, \begin{align*} &\frac{1}{\mu(B)^2}\int_B\int_B|f(x)-f(y)|^p\,d\mu(x)\,d\mu(y)\\ &\quad\lesssim\lambda^pr_B^p\phi(B)^{\gamma p}+\frac{\lambda^pr_B^p}{\mu(B)}\mathop{\int_{\Lambda B}\int_{\Lambda B}}\limits_{\genfrac{}{}{}{2}{|f(x)-f(y)|}{\rho(x,y)\phi(x,y)^\gamma}>\lambda}\frac{\phi(x,y)^{\gamma p}}{V(x,y)}\,d\mu(x)\,d\mu(y), \end{align*} where $V(x,y):=\mu(B(x,\rho(x,y)))$ and either $\phi=\rho$ with $\phi(B)=r_B$ and $\gamma\in(-\infty,-\frac{\min\{q,D\}}{p}]$ or $\phi=V$ with $\phi(B)=\mu(B)$ and $\gamma\in(-\infty,-\frac{q}{p\max\{q,d\}}]$. Here both ranges of $\gamma$ are sharp over the class of $q$-Poincar\'e spaces with the prescribed lower and upper dimensions, and the constant $\Lambda\in[1,\infty)$ and the implicit positive constant depend only on $p$, $\gamma$, and the geometric constants of $X$. We also obtain lower bounds for Sobolev energy and total variation in terms of the limit inferior of these functionals, for $\gamma$ in either the above negative ranges or $(0,\infty)$. Our proofs use the curve characterization of Poincar\'e spaces and an adaptive dyadic refinement argument based on medians.

papers.title: An infinite family of conservation laws for perfect compressible fluids
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of an infinite family of conservation laws and, more generally, balance laws, satisfied by plane-symmetric flows of perfect compressible fluids, allowing all components of the velocity vector to be possibly non-vanishing. We cover general pressure laws satisfying solely hyperbolicity and asymptotic conditions. We exhibit an almost quadratic formulation of the Euler equations, which we refer to as the J-formulation, and introduce a reduced Euler system based on an effective mass-energy density and an effective pressure law which account for transverse velocities. We establish the existence of a fundamental kernel which we use to generate all spacetime (quasi-)currents, also called mathematical entropy pairs. We derive explicit formulas for their density and flux components, together with the source-terms of the corresponding balance laws. Furthermore, we establish regularity and asymptotic estimates covering the whole range of physical variables, including vacuum. We prove that the kernel is positive on the interior of its support provided the pressure law satisfies a genuine nonlinearity condition, and we also investigate the future-convexity of the spacetime currents. Throughout, the fluid momentum parallel to the orbits of plane-symmetry is kept arbitrary. In turn, this family of spacetime quasi-currents provides a key ingredient in our companion study of torus-symmetric Einstein-Euler flows with weak regularity.

papers.title: A phenotype-structured Cahn-Hilliard model
papers.abstract: We propose a phenotype-structure form of the Cahn-Hilliard equation with degenerate mobility and analyze the existence of weak solutions for this new variant. This model is motivated by tumor modeling as multiple phenotypes co-exist within the same tumor and are believed to constitute a continuum of phenotypes. The originality of the model lies in its ability to consider an infinite number of phases and it allows for spatial interactions between phenotypes as well as transport in the phenotypic space, i.e., mutations.

papers.title: Quantitative Stability for Anisotropic Gaussian Isoperimetric Inequality
papers.abstract: We prove a sharp, dimension-free quantitative stability theorem for the Gaussian isoperimetric inequality in general Gauss spaces $(\mathbb{R}^n,\gamma_A)$, where $A$ is an arbitrary positive-definite matrix. More precisely, we show that the anisotropic Gaussian perimeter deficit controls the square of the anisotropic Gaussian asymmetry with a dimension-free constant, recovering the sharp quadratic stability behavior known in the isotropic setting. The central difficulties are the loss of rotational symmetry and the lack of compactness of the isoperimetric sets. The main novelty of our work is a new symmetrization-based reduction to the small-perturbation regime, together with effective Fuglede-type estimates derived from the weighted constant mean curvature equation. These ingredients overcome the principal obstructions created by anisotropy and extend the proof-from-regularity approach to quantitative isoperimetric stability in the anisotropic setting.

papers.title: Global strong solutions of the three-dimensional Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes system via finite-dimensional scalar forcing
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish global existence of strong solutions for the three-dimensional Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes system on the torus through finite-dimensional scalar modifications of a prescribed external force. For arbitrary initial data in $H^1\times H^2$ and any force that is locally bounded in time, we construct two smooth scalar corrections, one added to the third component of the fluid force and the other to the phase source. These corrections involve three fixed Fourier frequencies in the fluid equation and one in the phase equation, and act only on a set of times of arbitrarily small total measure. The proof combines a quantitative local theory with repeated returns of the solution to a fixed ball around zero. These returns rely on small-time asymptotic limits that balance the different scales of the two equations, together with a saturation procedure carefully adapted to the structure of the coupled system. Fluid transport generates the phase frequencies that the chosen phase forcing cannot produce on its own. As a consequence, we also obtain global strong solutions for the three-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations with a single smooth scalar correction acting on one component of the force at three fixed Fourier frequencies.

papers.title: Spectral Convergence of the Discrete Steklov Problem
papers.abstract: We study the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the Schur complement $\textbf{S}$ of the graph Laplacian, defined on vertices sampled from a domain with $C^2$ boundary. We use a thin boundary layer to approximate the continuum boundary as the number of vertices increases and rely on transportation theory to justify the consistency of a discrete Steklov problem. In particular, $\textbf{S}$ acts on vectors defined over the shrinking boundary layer but behaves asymptotically like a known operator. In this paper, we use a variational argument to determine conditions for which the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of $\textbf{S}$ converge to the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of a Dirichlet-to-Neumann map, and we provide evidence of this spectral convergence through a numerical example.

papers.title: Nondegeneracy of low-energy nodal solutions to the Yamabe equation
papers.abstract: We study the linearized Yamabe equation in $\R^n$, or equivalently on $\s^n$, at a low-energy sign-changing solution with two nodal domains. We consider odd dimensions $n=2k-1$ and a solution invariant under $\Gamma=O(k)\times O(k)$. Its regular level sets are isoparametric hypersurfaces, which foliate the sphere away from the two focal submanifolds. This symmetry reduces the equation for the solution to a singular ODE. In the balanced case, we choose a single-node profile that is odd under reflection across the midpoint. We prove nondegeneracy in the $\Gamma$-invariant subspace for every $k\ge2$, and in the full space $H^1(\s^n)$ for sufficiently large $k$: every kernel element is generated by a conformal invariance of the equation. The proof uses separation of variables, Wronskian identities and comparison functions adapted to the singular equations for the angular modes.

papers.title: Optimal design problems for the fractional $g$-Laplacian at prescribed energy level
papers.abstract: In this work we study two optimal design problems, of hard and soft obstacle type, in fractional Orlicz-Sobolev spaces. We also establish the connection between these problems, and finally we analyze the asymptotic behavior of the quotients $\Lambda_{s,\mu}(\alpha)/\mu$ with respect to the energy level $\mu$ at the endpoints $0$ and $+\infty$.

papers.title: On kinetic alignment models with rough communication kernel
papers.abstract: We prove the weak maximum principle and the Cucker-Smale flocking theorem for a general class of kinetic alignment models with rough communication kernels. This includes the classical Cucker-Smale and Motsch-Tadmor systems with defining kernel $\phi$ assumed to be merely continuous or even $\phi\in L^\infty$ for solutions in the Lebesgue class $f\in L^1$. For such models the characteristic flow-map is not well-defined and therefore the classical approaches of Cucker-Smale \cite{CS2007a,CS2007b} or Ha-Liu-Tadmor \cite{HL2009,HT2008} break down. We develop a new method adopted to rough settings based on Ambrossio's probabilistic representation of solutions and construction of dynamic barriers. All proofs are performed in the framework of so called bounded communication protocols, a non-smooth variant of regular protocols introduced in \cite{Shv-CPAM, Shv-EA} and representing a broad range of models of collective dynamics.

papers.title: Long-Time Behavior towards Generic Riemann Solutions for Radiative Euler Equations
papers.abstract: We study the time-asymptotic stability of generic Riemann solutions for the one-dimensional radiative Euler equations, where the Riemann pattern consists of a $1$-rarefaction wave, a $2$-contact discontinuity, and a $3$-shock wave. We prove that, for sufficiently small wave strengths and initial perturbations, the Cauchy problem admits a unique global solution, which converges uniformly as $t\to \infty$ to a composite wave of the $1$-rarefaction wave, $2$-viscous contact wave, and $3$-radiative shock profile with a time-dependent shift. As a key ingredient, we establish a comprehensive set of quantitative estimates for weak radiative shock profiles. Our proof is based on the method of $a$-contraction with shifts. In all previous applications of the $a$-contraction method to the study of long-time behavior, the proof has relied essentially on the parabolic structure provided by either viscosity or heat conduction. In this work, we extend the method to a hyperbolic-elliptic system without parabolic structure.

papers.title: Nonexistence of Stable Solutions to the Liouville Equation on Graphs with Polynomial Volume Growth
papers.abstract: We study stable solutions of the discrete Liouville equation \[ -\Delta u=e^u \] on infinite, locally finite graphs with polynomial volume growth. We prove that no stable solution exists whenever the order $d$ of polynomial volume growth satisfies $d<10$.

papers.title: Critical Optimizers for the Finite-Rank Fractional Lieb--Thirring Inequality
papers.abstract: We study optimal potentials for the finite-rank fractional Lieb--Thirring problem at the eigenvalue-counting endpoint, for \(0<s<1\) and \(d>2s\). Using the zero-energy Birman--Schwinger formulation, we prove a profile decomposition of normalized optimizing sequences with exact splitting of rank and potential mass, and strong approximation in \(L^{d/(2s)}\). Strict subadditivity yields existence and compactness modulo translations and dilations. At rank two, the optimal constant equals the rank-one constant, the supremum is not attained, and every normalized optimizing sequence splits into two Sobolev potentials. We also prove strict increase of the minimal potential masses and a uniform spectral gap for optimizing sequences. For each optimizer, we derive an Euler--Lagrange system and establish boundedness, local H\"older regularity and \(V(x)=|x|^{-4s}(c_\infty+o(1))\) as \(|x|\to\infty\), with \(c_\infty\geq0\). The conformal orbit of every optimizer contains a representative with a strictly positive asymptotic coefficient.

papers.title: On hot spots of the torsion function and the ground state of the Laplacian
papers.abstract: We compare the maximum points \(P_\Omega\) and \(Q_\Omega\) of the torsion function and the positive first Dirichlet eigenfunction. We begin with a systematic analytic description of both hot spots over the full range of opening angles of circular sectors: uniqueness, strict monotonicity with respect to the angle, distinct small-angle asymptotics, and explicit limiting equations in the slit-disk limit. We also prove the existence of a coincidence angle and establish arithmetic properties of the limiting coordinates. We then consider bounded convex planar domains with a line of symmetry, and we prove the sharp diameter-normalized identity \[ \sup_\Omega \frac{|P_\Omega-Q_\Omega|}{\operatorname{diam}(\Omega)}=\frac12. \] Its upper-bound argument uses standard localization in the heart and an elementary geometric enclosure. Sharpness follows from thin convex domains with a vanishing relative width perturbation peaking near one endpoint: the torsion hot spot approaches that endpoint, whereas the ground-state hot spot approaches the midpoint.

papers.title: Local Smoothing Estimates of Schr\"{o}dinger Operators on Waveguides Using Refined Decoupling
papers.abstract: We establish improved local smoothing estimates for the Schr\"odinger equation on waveguides. Our results extend the previously known range of exponents in every dimension and are sharp in certain cases. The proof develops a transference argument that preserves the discrete periodic frequency structure, together with a refined decoupling estimate adapted to waveguides. We also derive consequences for Euclidean local smoothing and almost everywhere convergence.

papers.title: Existence, Equivalence, and Convergence of Unbalanced Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: We study an unbalanced optimal transport problem with a spatially independent signed source. The target density is continuous on a bounded domain or continuous and integrable on $\mathbb R^n$. We establish sequential weak lower semicontinuity at the critical Sobolev regularity $W^{1,n}$ and existence of minimizers under prescribed distortion and Jacobian mass bounds, provided a finite-energy admissible pair exists. For domain-preserving, uniformly bi-Lipschitz affine flows, we prove an energy-preserving static-dynamic correspondence and stability of the reconstruction. Within this class, sequential $\Gamma$-convergence identifies the strong source-penalty limit as transport minimization among pairs of minimum source cost. This yields optimal-cost asymptotics and subsequential convergence of minimizers and their reconstructed paths. When a constant source is admissible, optimal sources converge strongly in $L^2$ to the constant determined by the endpoint mass difference. We establish local constant-source feasibility for H\"older endpoint densities near a fixed reference pair and give a quantitative obstruction showing that constant-source feasibility may fail even when admissible pairs exist.

papers.title: Exponential stability of port-Hamiltonian systems with unstructured, measurable Hamiltonian densities
papers.abstract: For first-order port-Hamiltonian systems in the dissipative setting considered here, we characterise exponential stability without any further regularity or block-structure assumption on the Hamiltonian density, thus closing a gap persisting in the literature. The proof requires revisiting the computation of the adjoint generator of the port-Hamiltonian semigroup. Finally, we provide both examples and non-examples showcasing the inconclusiveness of known conditions on the Hamiltonian densities necessary for the application of characterisation results in the literature.

papers.title: Integral Harnack-type estimates and the rate of extinction for nonlocal doubly nonlinear parabolic equations
papers.abstract: We establish local boundedness and integral Harnack-type inequalities for locally nonnegative weak solutions to nonlocal doubly nonlinear parabolic equations in the fast diffusion range by combining refined energy estimates with a careful treatment of the nonlocal terms. As an application, quantitative decay estimates for both the local mass and the local supremum of weak solutions are derived near the extinction time. Furthermore, we study the extinction phenomenon for bounded nonnegative weak solutions to the Cauchy--Dirichlet problem and obtain quantitative upper bounds for the extinction time.

papers.title: Finite-energy travelling waves for the easy-plane Landau-Lifshitz equation
papers.abstract: For every integer $d\ge2$ and every subsonic speed $c\in(0,1)$, we construct a nonconstant finite-energy travelling wave for the easy-plane Landau-Lifshitz equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$. This addresses the existence problem raised in the numerical work of Papanicolaou and Spathis. The profiles satisfy the travelling-wave equation in the sense of distributions and are smooth in dimension two.

papers.title: A lower bound for the stability constant in the Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg inequality
papers.abstract: We study the dependence on the dimension of stability constants for the Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg inequalities, using the weighted energy distance to the manifold of optimizers. In the subcritical non-degenerate case, i.e., $b_{FS}(a)<b<a+1$ with $a<0$ and $a<b<a+1$ with $a\ge0$, we prove \[ \frac{\beta_{a,b}}d\le c_{d,a,b} \le \frac{4(1+a-b)}{d+4(1+a-b)} \] with a positive constant depending only on the weights, uniformly over all admissible dimensions. The upper bound shows that this dimensional order is optimal. The critical case $a=b>0$ exhibits a different dimensional scale, \[ \frac{\min\{\beta_{\mathrm{Sob}},4a\}}{25d^2} \le c_{d,a,a}\le\frac{16a}{d^2}+O_a(d^{-3}), \] where $\beta_{\mathrm{Sob}}>0$ is a universal Sobolev stability constant. In the degenerate case on the Felli--Schneider curve, for fixed $a<0$, we prove \[ \frac{\beta_a^{FS}}{d^3} \le\widetilde c_{d,a,b_{FS}(a)} \le\frac{32|a|}{d^3}+O_a(d^{-4}), \] where $\widetilde c$ is the quartic stability constant given in [Frank-Peteranderl, CV\&PDE, 2024] and $\beta_a^{FS}>0$ is independent of $d$. The three cases thus have optimal dimensional orders $d^{-1}$, $d^{-2}$, and $d^{-3}$, respectively.

papers.title: On the Integrate-and-Fire model with superlinear drift
papers.abstract: The Nonlinear Integrate-and-Fire equation is a fundamental model for neural assemblies, describing the dynamics of the density of neurons with a given potential. Its standard formulation uses a given firing potential, and is known to undergo finite-time blow-up for excitatory connections. To fit experimental observations, it has been advocated to use superlinear drifts. We show how, in this situation, it makes sense to set the equation on the whole line. The main question we address is whether in these circumstances the solution still exhibits finite-time blow-up. We study the construction of solutions by a fixed point and, using the framework of \cite{carrilloQualitativePropertiesSolutions2015}, we develop novel a priori estimates which use specifically the superlinearity of the drift at $+\infty$. In particular, we obtain Ces{\`a}ro-mean bounds on the activity, as well as exponential convergence towards the unique steady state in the weakly connected regime. Several critical steps rely on controls depending solely on the $L^1$ norm of the solution or coefficients.

papers.title: An Onsager-type theorem for the compressible Euler equations
papers.abstract: For any $0\leq\gamma_m<\frac13$ and $0\leq\gamma_\rho<\frac23$,, we use convex integration to construct a nontrivial weak solution $(\rho,m)$ to the three-dimensional isentropic compressible Euler equations such that $\rho-\rho^*\in C^{\gamma_\rho}(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}^3)$ and $m\in C^{\gamma_m}(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}^3)$. Here $\rho^*>0$ is a constant, and the density stays bounded away from vacuum. Both $\rho-\rho^*$ and $m$ have compact support in time. The construction applies to smooth pressure laws with positive derivative throughout the density range. This yields nonuniqueness for the constant initial data $(\rho^*,0)$. Each stage of the convex integration scheme consists of finitely many Newton steps followed by a Nash step. Kirchhoff's formula in Lagrangian coordinates and the Piola transform yield coupled density and momentum corrections that treat the acoustic part of the linearized system while preserving the continuity equation exactly. In the Newton step, we combine these corrections with an incompressible correction adapted from Giri--Radu (2024) to reduce the error. In the Nash step, a divergence-free perturbation built from spatially separated Mikado flows treats the gluing stresses on disjoint time intervals without changing the density.

papers.title: Blow-up suppression for the 2D parabolic-parabolic Patlak-Keller-Segel-Navier-Stokes system
papers.abstract: Chemotactic aggregation can overcome diffusion and lead to finite-time blow-up in Patlak-Keller-Segel models. Mixing induced by suitable fluid flows can counteract this aggregation through enhanced dissipation. Earlier results of Zeng-Zhang-Zi (J. Funct. Anal., 2021) for the coupled system impose additional smallness assumptions on the initial chemical gradient. A natural question is whether this restriction can be removed for the coupled system near a stationary Couette flow. We give a positive answer to this question for the two-dimensional parabolic-parabolic Patlak-Keller-Segel-Navier-Stokes system near the Couette flow $(Ay,0)$ in $\mathbb T\times\mathbb R$. It is proved that, when the Couette flow is strong enough ($A$ is large enough), the system admits a global solution that remains uniformly bounded in time for arbitrary fixed initial data. The main difficulties are the transient growth of the chemical gradient and the nonlinear coupling among the density, chemical field and fluid. We develop a two-stage energy method combining short-time estimates in Kelvin coordinates with long-time estimates in physical coordinates. The key is to split the nonzero chemical modes into two parts while accounting for the nonlinear transport. One part carries the initial data, and the other is a forced component with zero initial data. A weighted coupled energy controls the former through a time-integrable Gronwall coefficient and absorbs the feedback from the latter without increasing the initial energy. Enhanced dissipation then provides the bounds needed to enter the long-time regime, while one-dimensional zero-mode estimates and Moser iteration complete the argument without a mass restriction.

papers.title: The virial--Kato method and the asymptotic stability of solitons of the generalized Benjamin, Bona and Mahony equation
papers.abstract: We apply to the generalized pure power Benjamin, Bona and Mahony equation our method of combining high energy virial estimates with Kato smoothing, which closes the virial estimates in a natural way and allows us to prove a result of asymptotic stability for all the stable solitons with $c>1$ for all the exponents $p>1$.

papers.title: Boundary stabilization of a moving interface in a 2 x 2 weakly hyperbolic system of balance laws: application to continuous sedimentation
papers.abstract: We design a boundary feedback for the level of the sediment bed of a continuous settler and prove that it exponentially stabilizes the linearized closed loop under a small-gain condition. The unit is modeled by a 2 x 2 system of balance laws in which the bed surface, the interface, is not a smooth part of the solution but a moving shock between a weakly hyperbolic free-settling zone and a strictly hyperbolic compression zone. We describe it by the Rankine-Hugoniot relations and map the problem onto a fixed domain. Moreover, we prove local well-posedness with a continuation criterion given by a single margin function. Then we linearize the system near an equilibrium. The linearization couples a dissipative distributed layer to one scalar, the interface position, whose equation does not contain the control. We solve this by infinitedimensional forwarding: a Sylvester kernel cancels the interface trace and isolates the interface pole, and a proportional feedback then sets its decay rate. Every hypothesis is verified on an illustrative example, a laboratory-scale continuous settler containing a bed of compact polystyrene beads.
